description: How much room is left, on both machines. The physical host answers 'can this box take another service', the LXC answers 'is the thing that is actually filling up going to fill up', and the Proxmox section answers 'is the thin pool about to become everyone's problem'.

panels.title: Load (1m) per core
panels.description: Above 1 means more runnable work than cores. The LXC's own 6-core quota is what throttles Ollama — see AGENTS.md on num_thread.

panels.title: Docker LXC — CT 100 (where everything actually runs)
CPU used
panels.description: The container's own view. Capped by a 6-core cgroup quota regardless of the host's 16 threads.

panels.title: Root filesystem used
panels.description: This is the number that fills. Docker images, Loki chunks, Prometheus TSDB and /opt/backups all live here, on a 400 GB rootfs sitting on a ~348 GiB thin pool that cannot auto-extend.

panels.title: Disk used by the biggest containers
panels.description: cAdvisor's per-container writable-layer usage. The usual suspects for an LXC that is filling up.

panels.title: Root filesystem free
panels.description: Trend, not level. A line heading for the floor at a steady rate is the thing to catch; the alert at 85% is the backstop.

panels.title: Proxmox storage used
panels.description: `local-lvm` is the thin pool. It is ~348 GiB and the CT 100 rootfs is provisioned at 400 GiB, so this can be exhausted while the guest still believes it has room — at which point writes fail inside the container.

panels.title: Media drive used
panels.description: The 5 TB drive at /mnt/media on m5, read by the host's node-exporter. 85% is where hl-disk-full fires. Empty means the exporter does not report this mount, and then no disk alert covers it either.

panels.title: Media drive used over time
panels.description: Last 30 days whatever the dashboard's range. A batch of downloads shows as a step; the slope between steps is how long the drive has left.

panels.title: Drive health (SMART, read nightly at 02:30)
panels.description: Written by scripts/host/hl-vzdump-hook after each nightly backup. Pending or uncorrectable above 0 means sectors the drive cannot read (hl-smart-pending pages); reallocated climbing week over week means it is wearing out (hl-smart-reallocating). Empty: the hook on m5 is an older copy (docs/runbook-backups.md, SMART metrics).

title: Homelab — Capacity & Headroom
